plain: To cancel or take back an order or law

webster.text: To abrogate; to revoke; to annul; to vacate an act by the enacting authority or by superior authority; as, to rescind a law, a resolution or a vote; to rescind an edict or decree; to rescind a judgment.

example.quote: A motion to rescind the order of the House respecting the hours of meeting & adjourning, was negatived:
example.cite: James Madison, Notes of Debates in the Federal Convention of 1787, August 22, 1787
